question: The Gita is incorporated in the Mahabharata primarily to give an integrated view of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhagavad Gita, often referred to simply as the Gita, is a 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the Indian epic Mahabharata.
 
• The Gita is primarily a conversation between Prince Arjuna and the god Krishna, who serves as his charioteer.
 
• This conversation takes place on the battlefield just before the Kurukshetra War, where Krishna imparts spiritual wisdom and guidance to Arjuna.
 
• The core theme of the Gita is "Dharma," which refers to the righteous path or duty. It emphasizes following one's duty according to one's role in life without attachment to the results.
 
• The Gita integrates various paths of yoga (devotion, action, and knowledge) to explain the concept of Dharma and the importance of righteous living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dharma:** In Hinduism, Dharma signifies behaviors that are considered to be in accord with the order that makes life and the universe possible, including duties, rights, laws, conduct, virtues, and "right way of living".
 
• **Kurukshetra War:** The epic battle depicted in the Mahabharata, fought between two groups of cousins, the Kauravas and the Pandavas, for the throne of Hastinapura.
 
• **Krishna:** A major deity in Hinduism, worshipped as the eighth avatar of the god Vishnu and also as the supreme God in his own right. In the Gita, Krishna serves as Arjuna's charioteer and guide.
 
• **Yoga:** The Gita discusses various paths of yoga (Bhakti Yoga, Karma Yoga, and Jnana Yoga) as ways to realize one's spiritual duties and align with Dharma.
 
• **Mahabharata:** One of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the struggle for sovereignty between the Kauravas and the Pandavas.
